text:
maria: FYI we started seeing a tokens/sec regression after flipping the tiled FlashAttention path for long contexts (4k+). baseline (paged) was ~1.2k tps, tiled flash is ~950 tps and cost/M went up. Can we triage?

ashwin: Thanks — repro steps? I ran a quick microbench.
ashwin: Command I used:
```bash
run_profiling --model llama-2-13b --seq 4096 --batch 1 --kernel flash-tiled --iters 200
```
ashwin: Key numbers (median over last 50 iters):
- tokens/sec: 960
- GPU util avg: 78%
- kernel hotspot: attention_tiled_kernel (48% time)
- memcpy overhead: 7%

jenn: ouch. baseline tiled-vs-paged? iirc paged was lower latency for 1k-2k but better throughput at 4k+?

ashwin: Baseline paged run on same machine (same seeds):
- tokens/sec: 1,210
- GPU util avg: 72%
- attention_paged kernel: 41% time
- memcpy overhead: 4%

kai: Interesting that tiled has higher GPU util but lower tps. Could be extra work per token (tiling overhead) or more cache churn. Did you check KV cache hit patterns?

maria: I dumped KV stats from the runtime for tiled vs paged. Short summary: tiled path shows ~8% extra KV writes per step and more frequent buffer reallocs.

ashwin: paste of profiler flame (simplified):
```text
- forward_total: 11.2 ms
  - attention_tiled_kernel: 5.4 ms
  - softmax + transpose: 2.0 ms
  - kv_write: 1.8 ms
  - misc (memcpy/alloc): 1.2 ms
```

sam: allocation churn stands out — if tiled path allocs temp tiles each step we pay allocator cost, fragmentation, and extra memcpy. Did we switch alloc policy in that PR?

jenn: @ashwin can you attach the allocator trace? Also include peak mem and number of realloc calls.

ashwin: allocator trace snippet (counts are per-batch-step averages):
```text
realloc_calls: 3.1
new_allocs_temp: 4.7
peak_buffer_count: 12
```

kai: Another angle: batching heuristics. With tiled we changed the auto-batcher to prefer wider tiles which reduces batch packing density for multi-request workloads. That increases per-token overhead for small concurrent requests -> lowers effective tps under our traffic shape.

maria: We saw a ~6% throughput loss when running 8x small concurrent requests vs single large batch. Could be the bin-packing change.

ashwin: I ran a cost calc tied to tokens/sec change:
- baseline paged: 1,210 tps => $/M tokens = $0.47 (approx, based on our infra cost model)
- tiled flash: 960 tps => $/M tokens = $0.59
So ~25% higher unit cost.

maria: That delta matters for Dedicated customers (they care about $/M). We need to decide whether tiled flash is a net win across our workload distribution.

kai: Proposal: add a runtime kernel selector policy that chooses paged vs tiled based on sequence length + concurrent request packing score + alloc-churn heuristic. If seq >= 6k pick tiled, if concurrent small requests pick paged.

jenn: That selector sounds good. Also we should optimize tiled to avoid temp alloc each step: try reusing a pre-allocated tile buffer keyed by max tile shape, and move ephemeral allocations to a scratch pool.

ashwin: Agree. Quick experiments: reusing tile buffer reduced memcpy by ~50% and bumped tokens/sec from 960 to ~1,050 in a single-run test. Not back to paged but close.

maria: Nice. Action items:
1) ashwin: add allocator + KV write telemetry to the perf dashboard (KV write rate, realloc calls) — due EOD Weds
2) kai: prototype kernel selector policy and add sim for our traffic mix — due Friday
3) jenn: PR to change tiled kernel to use scratch pool for temp buffers, bench after — due Thu
4) sam: run long-run stability test (12h) with tiled+scratch to check for memory fragmentation leaks — due next week

ops-bot: deploy/1234 to eng-runtime/flash-kernel A/B started by @maria at 1792106900 :rocket:

maria: tagging @product because unit cost change will affect pricing decks.

kai: quick note — if we keep tiled for >4k contexts only we should also update model-selection heuristics so hosted API pins model variant appropriately.

sam: will take a look at long-run logs after ashwin's telemetry lands.

jenn: small nit: add a perf-test to CI that runs seq=4096 batch=1 and records tokens/sec so this doesn't regress silently.

maria: Agreed. Thanks all. I'll sync results Friday morning in this thread. :thumbsup:
